title: Plate tectonics theory
competency: Explain the plate tectonics theory and identify the major continental and oceanic plates.

keywords.def: The rigid outer layer: the crust plus the uppermost mantle, about 0–100 km deep.
The weak, plastic layer of the mantle under the lithosphere, on which plates slide.
The theory that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the asthenosphere.
The zone where two plates meet: convergent, divergent or transform.

en.text: Plate tectonics (late 1960s) says the lithosphere, the rigid crust and uppermost mantle, is broken into about a dozen large plates and some small ones. They slide a few centimetres a year over the weak, plastic asthenosphere and meet at plate boundaries. Plate edges are not the edges of continents: a plate can be continental, oceanic or both.

screens.title: Does Africa's plate end at its coast?
screens.ask: Is the edge of the African Plate the same as the coast of Africa?
opts: No, the plate also includes ocean floor around Africa
screens.after: The African Plate reaches the mid-Atlantic ridge and other ocean ridges. Plate edges do not follow coastlines.

screens.title: Lithosphere and asthenosphere
paras: Lithosphere: crust + uppermost mantle, rigid, about 0–100 km.
Asthenosphere: weak, plastic, partly molten layer beneath it.
The lithosphere slides over the asthenosphere.

screens.title: The theory
paras: About a dozen large plates plus smaller ones.
They move a few cm per year and change size.
Plates can be continental, oceanic or both.
They meet at plate boundaries, where mountains, earthquakes and volcanoes form.
It also affects the oceans, the atmosphere and long-term climate.

screens.text: About how fast do plates move?
